# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: The strategy in the first round was to look at the shape of the animal and give it the name of the animal. Initially we added man at the end but for the second round, we dropped the man and just went with the animal. For round 3 and up, we just use color names. We looked at unique colors each image possessed and used those names to label. The strategy changed when the images moved from easily identifiable animals to abstract robot images. The criteria used for naming changed from using animal names to specific color names.

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value:
For the lego characters, we decided to differentiate them based on the direction their hair was pointing, its colours, and the colour of their feet. 
During the last round with the black figures we figured they resembled human figures in either kneeling or standing poses. However, this only split the 8 images up into two separate categories and we ran out of time before we could further differentiate them. So we simply did our best to memorize the number associated with each image and wrote the number after they appeared to be standing or kneeling.

prompt_mistake.value: During the first three rounds we made no mistakesour scheme of describing the figures was strong enough that we were able to differentiate each one specifically. The last round though was a doozy, we didn't figure out an adequate scheme to differentiate the figures so we basically attempted to remember which figure was numbered and wrote the number we remembered instead of any real system of naming.

prompt_strategy.value: I think we both just tried to come up with things that we would easily relate to what we saw and tried to keep the words simple. My partner was definitely better at coming up with easier things to remember whereas I think sometimes I went a little too complex. It was definitely easier when we came up with simple things and there would be a memory there that would make us laugh so it made it easier to remember.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake

prompt_mistake.value: I mixed up dead and pray in the final ones. My partner got it correct and I muddled them which was hard to then guess whether he would then change his answer to match mine and I tried to match his. But other than that I think we remembered well. In the practice round there was a miscommunication on my part so I thought he'd said something else. But then we realised that could be an issue and were very clear after that.
